dataset.name: Plant physiological and climate data for Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE) site at Sabana Field Research Station, Luquillo, Puerto Rico from 2015-2017
description: This data publication includes all data used in data analysis in publication assessing physiological acclimation of the understory shrubs at the Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Eexperiment (TRACE), located at the Sabana Field Research Station in the Luquillo Experimental Forest, Puerto Rico. Physiological acclimation was assessed on two understory shrubs, Psychotria brachiata and Piper glabrescens, through photosynthetic and respiratory temperature response curves measured at four time points: January 2016, August 2016, January-February 2017, and June 2017. Supplemental physiology data were collected throughout the study period, including stomatal morphology and measures of the photosynthetic biochemical responses to temperature. Complementary environmental data were collected by TRACE describing surface temperature, air temperature, relative humidity, and soil moisture within the experimental plots. Environmental conditions underneath the canopy and rainfall were also collected and used for the study. The dataset includes approximately two years of environmental measurements of the field site and 1.5 years of physiology measurements. Also included are data analyses R code used in Carter et al. (2020).

measurementTechnique:
STUDY DESIGN
The study was conducted at the Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE) site located at the Luquillo Experimental Forest. The TRACE is comprised of three heated and three control 4 meter (m)-diameter plots located in the forest understory. The heated plots (initiated September 2016) were warmed +4 °C using six infrared (IR) heating panels, each positioned in a hexagonal ring and raised approximately 2.6 m above the ground. Control plots had identical infrastructure, but with no electrical power cabling and non-heated black metal panels instead of IR panels. See Kimball et al. (2018) for more detail of experimental design and infrastructure.
Gas exchange temperature responses curves were measured during four measurements campaigns. Two prior to initiation to the warming treatment, January 2016 (Winter) and August 2016 (Summer), and two after the warming was initiated, January 2017 (Winter) and May/early June 2017 (Summer). Stomatal traits were measured during August 2016, January 2017, and June 2017. Measurements were collected on the first fully expanded leaf of the two most common woody species found in the plots, Psychotria brachiata and Piper glabrescens. Stomatal traits were collected on the same leaf as gas exchange measurements except during June 2017. The leaves marked as “old” leaves were the same leaves as the gas exchange measurements. The leaves marked as “new” were new leaves that fully developed under the warming treatment. They were fully expanded but did not have full development of chlorophyll.
Two to four leaves of each species were sampled in each plot on separate plants during each measurement campaign. When there were not enough plants in an individual plot, extra leaves were collected in a separate plot of the same treatment. There were some cases where there were not enough individual plants to get an adequate sample size. When this occurred, two leaves were collected from the same plant. This is indicated in the “Leaf” column of in the physiology datasheets.
DATA COLLECTION - PLANT PHYSIOLOGY
Infrared gas analyzer: LI6400 (Li-Cor Inc., Lincoln, NE, United States) was used for all gas exchange measurements. The temperature of the chamber was adjusted outside of the normal instrumental range by cycling hot or cold water through the Expanded Temperature Control Kit (6400-88, Li-Cor Inc.) (see Carter et al. 2020 for more details). Net photosynthetic (Anet) temperature response curves were collected using the 2 x 3 cm head, collected measurements at 20, 25, 27, 30, 33, 35, 37, and 40 °C leaf temperature. CO₂ concentration was controlled 400 parts per million (ppm). Aci curves were also measured with a 2 x 3 cm head (6400-02B, Li-Cor Inc.) at leaf temperatures of 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 °C. Aci curves were constructed by measuring net photosynthesis at 400, 300, 200, 100, 50, 0, 450, 600, 850, 1000, and 1200 ppm CO₂ concentrations. For both Anet and Aci measurements, light was controlled at 800 micromoles per square meter per second (μmol m-2 s-1), and flow was controlled to keep vapor pressure deficit between 1 and 4 kilopascal (kPa). Measurements were conducted between the hours of 8am and 4pm. Respiratory temperature response curves were collected using a 6400-088 conifer chamber wrapped in aluminum foil. Curves were constructed by measuring CO₂ exchange of each leaf at 25, 30, 35, 37, and 40 °C. CO₂ concentrations were controlled at 400 ppm. Measurements were collected at nighttime between 7pm and 2am (see Carter et al. 2020 for more details).
Stomatal morphology: Stomatal size and density was measured by taking stomatal impressions of leaves using clear nail varnish on the abaxial side of the leaf. Impressions were taped to a glass microscope slide. Photos of impressions were taking at 20x times magnification using a compound light microscope (Eclipse 400, Nikon Instruments Inc., Melville, NY, United States) with a camera (DFC295, Leica Microsystems Inc., Buffalo Grove, IL, United States) fitted with a 55X coupler.
DATA COLLECTION - ENVIRONMENTAL
Surface/vegetation temperature: Surface temperature of the plots were continuously measured from July 2015 - August 2017 using infrared thermometers (SI-121, Apogee Instruments, Logan, UT), which measure temperature at an 18 degree half angle field of view.
Soil moisture: Soil moisture was measured using soil moisture probes (CS655, Campbell Scientific, Logan, UT, United States). Shallow soil moisture probes (0-10 centimeters [cm]) were installed in July 2015 and continuously recorded soil moisture every hour. Three shallow soil moisture probes were installed in each plot one each at the edge, center, and midway between the edge and center. Deeper soil moisture probes were installed in the plots at 20-30 cm and 40-50 cm depth in April 2016.
Air temperature: Below canopy air temperature (CS215, Campbell Scientific) was measured at a meteorological station (MET) at close proximity to the experimental warming plots. Air temperature and relative humidity was also measured in each plot at ~ 1 meter height using dataloggers (MX2391, Onset Computer Corp., Bourne, MA, United States) from June 20 - August 31, 2017.
Rainfall: Rainfall was collected as daily sums from two rainfall gauges in close proximity to the experimental site. The Sabana rainfall gauge was located in an open canopy just outside of the experimental plots. A second rainfall measurement was collected at the Bisley tower weather station located approximately 2 kilometer (km) from the TRACE site. Rainfall was collected using a 10 cm plastic funnel draining into a 180 milliliter (ml) plastic bottle. More information on Sabana and Bisley MET station measurements are provided in González (2017).
For more information about the collection of these data see Carter et al. (2020).
